title: Cross-attention driven RGBD fusion in lightweight CNN–Transformer for real-time stress classification of seedlings during robotic transplanting

facts.statement: The study proposes a lightweight RGBD multimodal framework for six-level stress classification of bell pepper seedlings.
facts.limits: Single crop species (bell pepper); six stress levels defined by water/nutrient regimens.

sources.quote: we propose a lightweight RGBD (RGB and depth) multimodal framework for six-level stress classification of bell pepper seedlings.

facts.statement: The framework integrates a dual-stream CNN–Transformer architecture with hierarchical cross-attention modules fusing RGB color-texture cues and depth-derived geometric cues at shallow and deep feature layers.
facts.limits: Architecture description; fusion is at feature layers via cross-attention.

sources.quote: Our approach integrates a dual-stream CNN–Transformer architecture in which hierarchical cross-attention modules fuse color-texture cues from the RGB stream with depth-derived geometric cues at both shallow and deep feature layers.

facts.statement: A dedicated dataset of 1537 paired RGBD images was collected with an oblique-view sensor during the pick-and-place cycle.
facts.limits: Dataset size and acquisition context; oblique-view sensor.

sources.quote: a dedicated dataset of 1537 paired RGBD images was collected with an oblique-view sensor during the pick-and-place cycle.

facts.statement: Deployed on an edge device, the network achieves an overall accuracy of 95.8% and maintains 5.2 frames per second when integrated into the parallel transplant-control pipeline.
facts.limits: Edge-device deployment; FPS measured under integration with transplant-control pipeline.

sources.quote: Deployed on an edge-device, the network achieves an overall accuracy of 95.8 % and maintains 5.2 frames per second when integrated into the parallel transplant-control pipeline.

facts.statement: Ablation studies show effective fusion of RGBD channel can improve accuracy by 4.9% over RGB-only baseline model.
facts.limits: Ablation context; comparison to RGB-only baseline.

sources.quote: Ablation studies reveal that effective fusion of RGBD channel can improve accuracy by 4.9 % over RGB-only baseline model.

facts.statement: The six stress treatment conditions are defined by watering interval (2, 4, or 6 days) and nutrient supply interval (2, 4, or 6 days, or None), denoted as W2N2, W2N0, W4N4, W4N0, W6N6, W6N0.
facts.limits: Treatment definitions; W2N2 is control with standard regimen every 2 days.

sources.quote:
|  | W2N2 | W2N0 | W4N4 | W4N0 | W6N6 | W6N0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Watering interval (day) | 2 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 6 | 6 |
| Nutrient supply interval (day) | 2 | None | 4 | None | 6 | None |

facts.statement: Seedlings were cultivated in 36-hole trays with coconut coir in an indoor incubator at 27°C, 70% relative humidity, and 15 h simulated daylight per day.
facts.limits: Controlled indoor environment; substrate and tray type specified.

sources.quote: The cultivation environment was maintained in an indoor incubator with a controlled temperature of 27 ◦C, relative humidity set at 70 %, and 15 h of simulated daylight provided each day.

facts.statement: The embedded platform is Jetson AGX Xavier (8-core ARM CPU, 512-core CUDA GPU, up to 32 TOPS) controlling a robotic arm and force-feedback gripper, with an Azure Kinect DK RGBD camera.
facts.limits: Hardware specification; platform and camera models named.

sources.quote: The hardware configuration of the seedling transplant system is built using the Jetson AGX Xavier (NVIDIA Corporation, Santa Clara, CA, USA), an embedded AI platform equipped with an 8-core ARM CPU and 512-core CUDA GPU, capable of delivering up to 32 TOPS for real-time inference.

facts.statement: The camera captured synchronized high-resolution RGB images (4096×3072 pixels) and aligned depth maps (640×576 pixels) at 5 frames per second.
facts.limits: Capture resolution and frame rate; RGB and depth resolutions differ.

sources.quote: The camera captured synchronized high-resolution RGB images (4,096 × 3072 pixels) and aligned depth maps (640 × 576 pixels) at 5 frames per second.

facts.statement: Camera-to-subject distance was fixed at 30 cm, slightly exceeding the minimum depth sensing range of 25 cm specified by the hardware.
facts.limits: Distance fixed; relative to hardware minimum depth range.

sources.quote: the camera-to-subject distance was fixed at 30 cm, slightly exceeding the minimum depth sensing range of 25 cm specified by the hardware.

facts.statement: The camera mounting configuration was set at a 35° oblique angle, determined through kinematic simulation and empirical tuning.
facts.limits: Angle determined by simulation and tuning; oblique view.

sources.quote: Fig. 1c depicts the optimized camera mounting configuration set at a 35◦ oblique angle, which was determined through kinematic simulation and empirical tuning.

facts.statement: Data augmentation applied to RGB images included horizontal flipping and random brightness/contrast adjustment within [0.8, 1.2]; aligned depth maps were only flipped horizontally when the paired RGB image was flipped.
facts.limits: Augmentation types and ranges; depth augmentation limited to horizontal flip.

sources.quote: These techniques included horizontal flipping and random adjustment to brightness and contrast within a range of [0.8, 1.2], simulating varying lighting environments. The aligned depth map was merely flipped horizontally whenever its paired RGB image was flipped; no brightness or contrast operations

facts.statement: A total of 2769 image samples were utilized, comprising 1537 original images and 1232 generated images using data augmentation; dataset partitioned into training and testing subsets using an 8:2 split ratio.
facts.limits: Total samples include augmented; split ratio 8:2.

sources.quote: A total of 2769 image samples were utilized in this study, comprising 1537 original images collected through field acquisition and 1232 generated images using data augmentation. For each experimental group, the dataset was randomly partitioned into training and testing subsets using an 8:2 split ratio.

facts.statement: The RGB-CTA baseline uses a tokenizer with two CRP modules (Conv2d 7×7, ReLU, MaxPool2d 3×3) with output channels 64 and 256, downsampling 224×224×C input to 14×14×256, followed by 7 transformer encoders, layer normalization, attention pooling, weighted averaging, and an MLP classifier.
facts.limits: Architecture details for baseline; input size 224×224×C.

sources.quote: Each CRP module consists of the following components: a 2D convolutional layer (Conv2d) with a kernel size of 7 × 7 and a 3 × 3 padding, a ReLU activation function to introduce non-linearity, and a 2D max-pooling layer (MaxPool2d) with a kernel size of 3 and padding of 1, which reduces the image size by half. CRP[0] and CRP[1] differ in their output channel sizes, which are 64 and 256, respectively.

facts.statement: The cross-attention module uses RGB features as query and depth features as key and value; output F is softmax((W^Q R)(W^K D)^T / sqrt(d)) D W^1, and fused feature C = F + R.
facts.limits: Fusion direction RGB-as-query; formula defines fusion.

facts.statement: Training used batch size 32, initial learning rate 5×10^{-4} with cosine annealing to minimum 1×10^{-5}, AdamW optimizer with weight decay 6×10^{-2}, learning rate warm-up from 1×10^{-6} over first 10 epochs, total 200 epochs, label smoothing 0.1, and automatic mixed precision.
facts.limits: Training configuration; optimizer and schedule specified.

sources.quote: The training process was configured with a batch size of 32 and an initial learning rate of 5 × 10−4, which was scheduled using cosine annealing with a minimum threshold of 1×10−5. The optimizer adopted was AdamW, incorporating a weight decay coefficient of 6 × 10−2.

facts.statement: An 80%/20% hold-out strategy combined with stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the training portion was used; 20% of the entire RGBD dataset was sequestered as an unseen test set accessed only once for final evaluation.
facts.limits: Validation strategy; test set accessed once.

sources.quote: we adopted an 80 %/20 % hold–out strategy combined with stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the training portion. Specifically, 20 % of the entire RGBD dataset was sequestered as an unseen test set and accessed only once for the final evaluation reported.

facts.statement: RGBD-CTA-F achieved accuracy 95.8%, precision 95.8%, recall 95.7%, F1-score 95.8%, 23.2 M params, 10.3 GFLOPs, 5.2 FPS; RGB-CTA baseline achieved 90.9% accuracy, 18.1 M params, 8.2 GFLOPs, 7.6 FPS; RGBD-CTA-D achieved 91.2% accuracy, 18.4 M params, 8.6 GFLOPs, 7.4 FPS.
facts.limits: Performance metrics on test set; FPS measured on Jetson AGX Xavier with PyTorch FP32 inference, batch 1, averaged over 100 test images including preprocessing and parallel control threads.
